title: JWT / bearer token
summary: alg=none, key confusion, unverified signatures, kid/jku tricks, role claims, expiry, and tokens in URLs.

groups.title: Signature and algorithm
groups.summary: If the signature is not verified, nothing else matters.

checks.title: alg=none
checks.why: The resource server accepts an unsecured JWT.
checks.validate: A token with alg=none and an empty signature is accepted as you.

variants.name: none with empty sig
variants.payload: Header: {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}\nPayload: copy a real token's claims, keep sub\nSignature: (empty)
variants.expect: Authorization: Bearer <header>.<payload>.   — trailing dot, empty sig. Must 401.
variants.why: Signing an arbitrary payload with alg=none and an empty signature bypasses verification.

variants.name: None / NONE / nOnE
variants.payload: {"alg":"None"}\n{"alg":"NONE"}\n{"alg":"nOnE"}
variants.expect: Case tricks. Same 401 expectation.
variants.why: The alg check may be case-sensitive, so casing variants bypass an exact-string deny.

checks.title: HS256 with the RSA public key
checks.why: The server is configured for RS256 but will verify HS256 using the PEM public key as the HMAC secret.
checks.validate: A token you signed with HS256 and the published public key is accepted. Use a test account.

variants.name: RS256 → HS256
variants.payload: Take the realm's public key (JWKS or TLS). Sign a test-account token with HS256 using that PEM as the secret.
variants.expect: Must 401. A 200 on /me as that account is the finding.
variants.why: Switching from RS256 to HS256 lets you sign with the public key as the HMAC secret.

variants.name: alg allowlist
variants.payload: Try alg=HS256, HS384, HS512 against an RS256 API, and EdDSA / PS256 if you have keys.
variants.expect: Only the configured algorithms may verify.
variants.why: A server that checks only the claimed alg but not a fixed allowlist is the confusion vector.

checks.title: Signature not checked
checks.why: Any well-formed three-part token is trusted.
checks.validate: A token with a garbage signature is accepted.

variants.name: Flip the last byte
variants.payload: Take a valid access token, change the last signature character, send it.
variants.expect: Must 401. If /me still returns you, signatures are not checked.
variants.why: A corrupted signature that is still accepted means verification is skipped.

variants.name: Empty payload claims only
variants.payload: Craft a token with sub= of another test account and a random signature.
variants.expect: Must 401. Do not target a real user.
variants.why: Tokens carrying only benign claims are the cleanest test that no signature is required.

checks.title: kid / jku / x5u controlled keys
checks.why: kid is used as a path or SQL key, or jku/x5u fetches an attacker JWKS.
checks.validate: A token signed with a key you control is accepted, or kid triggers a callback / traversal.

variants.name: jku to your JWKS
variants.payload: {"alg":"RS256","jku":"https://unique.oast.example/jwks.json","kid":"wapt"}
variants.expect: An outbound fetch to your listener is a lead. Acceptance of a token signed by that key is the finding. Do not point jku at cloud metadata.
variants.why: Pointing jku at an attacker JWKS supplies the key the server uses to verify.

variants.name: kid path / SQLi
variants.payload: {"kid":"../../wapt-canary.txt"}\n{"kid":"wapt' OR '1'='1"}\n{"kid":"http://unique.oast.example/key"}
variants.expect: Must be an allowlisted key id. A file read, SQL error, or callback is the finding.
variants.why: kid is often used as a file path or SQL key, enabling path traversal or injection.

variants.name: embedded jwk
variants.payload: {"alg":"RS256","jwk":{...your public key...}}
variants.expect: Embedded JWK must be ignored. A token signed by the matching private key must 401.
variants.why: A jwk embedded in the header can supply the verification key inline.

groups.title: Claims and transport
groups.summary: Roles, expiry, and where the token travels.

checks.title: Untrusted role / tenant claims
checks.why: The API trusts role, admin, or tenant_id inside a token the client can obtain or mint.
checks.validate: Raising a claim in a still-valid signature (or an accepted alg=none token) grants privilege.

variants.name: Raise role in a forged token
variants.payload: If alg=none or confusion worked, set role=admin / isAdmin=true / tenant_id of B and call an admin route.
variants.expect: Even if crypto held, try the same claims on a /me PATCH — mass assignment is the sibling finding.
variants.why: A forged role/tenant claim that is honoured is an authorization bypass.

variants.name: azp / aud / typ mix-up
variants.payload: Replay an id_token as an access token, or an access token issued for a sibling API.
variants.expect: aud and typ must be checked. A 200 on the wrong audience is the finding.
variants.why: Mismatched audience/type fields are parsed differently by client and server.

checks.title: exp / nbf enforced
checks.why: An expired access token or a reused refresh token still works.
checks.validate: A token past exp is accepted, or a rotated refresh token is replayed.

variants.name: Expired access token
variants.payload: Save an access token, wait for exp (or edit exp if signatures are not checked), replay /me.
variants.expect: Must 401. Clock skew of a minute is normal; hours are not.
variants.why: An accepted expired token means expiry is not enforced.

variants.name: Refresh replay
variants.payload: Refresh once, then replay the old refresh token.
variants.expect: The family must die. A second access token is the finding.
variants.why: Replaying a used refresh token means rotation is not enforced.

checks.title: JWT in the URL
checks.why: access_token= in a query, a hash fragment left in history, or a token in Referer.
checks.validate: A live token is observable in a URL, log, or Referer you are allowed to read.

variants.name: Token in query
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/me?access_token=<token> HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: If it works, the token is now in logs and Referer. Prefer that it does not work.
variants.why: A bearer in the query leaks into logs, caches, and Referer.

variants.name: Storage
variants.payload: DevTools → Application: localStorage / sessionStorage keys that hold a JWT.
variants.expect: A long-lived access token in localStorage is XSS→account takeover. Prefer memory or a cookie with the right flags.
variants.why: A token stored in accessible browser storage is readable by any script on the origin.

checks.title: Server rejects unexpected JWT algorithms
checks.why: Verification must pin the expected algorithm family from configuration, not read it from the token header.
checks.validate: Every token signed with an algorithm outside the configured set is rejected with 401, and the failure is logged.

variants.name: RS256 service, HS256 token
variants.payload: Take a valid RS256-issued token. Rebuild it with alg=HS256, signing the header.payload with the service RSA public key (the classic confusion probe).
variants.expect: Must 401. Acceptance means the verifier uses the header algorithm and trusts a public key as an HMAC secret.
variants.why: The header now names both the algorithm family and, effectively, the key material.

variants.name: Register an unsigned none token
variants.payload: Submit a token whose header is {"alg":"none"} with an empty signature segment, payload unchanged.
variants.expect: Must 401. No configuration accepts none in production.
variants.why: alg=none removes integrity entirely; rejecting it is the oldest JWT rule.

variants.name: Unexpected ECDSA alg
variants.payload: With ES256 configured, submit a valid RS256 token from the same issuer.
variants.expect: Must 401 with an algorithm-mismatch log line, not a generic decode error.
variants.why: Algorithm allowlists also catch cross-family confusion between asymmetric schemes.

checks.title: HMAC secrets resist guessing
checks.why: A guessable HMAC secret turns token signing into an open door: anyone can mint valid tokens offline.
checks.validate: The token does not verify with any dictionary secret, and the secret length/entropy meets policy (>= 256 bits random).

variants.name: Documentation secrets
variants.payload: Verify the header.payload signature with the obvious candidates: secret, jwt-secret, your-256-bit-secret, <app-name>, changeme.
variants.expect: None verify. Any hit is critical: forge a benign sub=<test-account> token to confirm, then report.
variants.why: Default and documentation secrets are the first thing an attacker tries.

variants.name: Offline HMAC check
variants.payload: echo -n '<header>.<payload>' | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac 'secret' — compare with the token's signature base64url-encoded.
variants.expect: Openssl output matches the signature only if that secret was used. Repeat per candidate.
variants.why: A local digest check proves which secret signed a captured token without touching the server.

variants.name: Crack-time note
variants.payload: If the secret is not guessable, estimate cost: hashcat -m 16500 token.txt <wordlist> against your own captured test token, time-boxed.
variants.expect: A full wordlist run finds nothing in the engagement window; record the estimate as evidence of strength.
variants.why: Show the secret is outside dictionary space rather than asserting it.

checks.title: jku, x5u, and embedded JWK headers rejected
checks.why: Key-location headers let a token bring its own verification key — an attacker-signed token that verifies itself.
checks.validate: Tokens carrying jku, x5u, x5c, or jwk header parameters are rejected unless the value matches a pre-registered allowlist.

variants.name: jku to Collaborator
variants.payload: Re-sign your test token with a fresh keypair; set jku to a URL you control (Burp Collaborator) hosting the matching JWK set.
variants.expect: Must 401 AND no outbound fetch may hit the Collaborator URL — an SSRF-grade key fetch is itself reportable.
variants.why: The verifier must never fetch keys from a URL named inside the token.

variants.name: x5u certificate URL
variants.payload: Same probe with x5u pointing at your HTTPS endpoint serving a self-signed certificate chain.
variants.expect: Must 401 without fetching. Certificate-chain fetch from token input is the same flaw.
variants.why: x5u is jku in certificate clothing.

variants.name: Embedded jwk header
variants.payload: Place your public JWK directly in the header ({"jwk":{...}}) and sign with the paired private key.
variants.expect: Must 401. An embedded key that verifies its own token is self-signed trust.
variants.why: Embedded keys are only acceptable when matched against a registered key set, never used blindly.

checks.title: Key rotation without unsafe fallback
checks.why: Rotation windows create fallback paths; a stale kid must never silently fall back to "whatever key we have".
checks.validate: An unknown kid, or a kid older than the rotation grace period, is rejected with a specific key-resolution error.

variants.name: Unknown kid
variants.payload: Submit an otherwise-valid token whose header kid does not exist in the current JWK set.
variants.expect: Must 401 with a key-resolution failure, not a signature retry against every key.
variants.why: Try-all-keys fallback enables kid confusion and cross-tenant key abuse.

variants.name: Pre-rotation key after grace
variants.payload: If a rotation is available or observed, keep a token signed with the retired key and replay it after the documented grace period.
variants.expect: Must 401 once the grace window closes; document the observed window.
variants.why: Grace periods exist for clock skew, not for permanent dual-trust.

variants.name: kid injection characters
variants.payload: Set kid to ../../rust-key or SQL-ish values and observe error handling.
variants.expect: Rejected as invalid key id; no path traversal, SQL, or LDAP-style resolution behaviour.
variants.why: kid is untrusted input to a key lookup — it must be treated as an identifier, not an expression.

checks.title: Issuer checked against a trust set
checks.why: A correctly signed token from the wrong issuer (another environment, another tenant IdP) must not grant access here.
checks.validate: iss equals the single configured issuer exactly (scheme, host, port); everything else is a 401.

variants.name: Sibling environment issuer
variants.payload: Take a valid token from staging (or another tenant IdP) and use it against production.
variants.expect: Must 401. Cross-environment acceptance is a full auth bypass.
variants.why: Signature validity is per-issuer; trust must be pinned per service.

variants.name: iss prefix tricks
variants.payload: Edit iss to https://idp.example.com.evil.test or https://evil.test/idp.example.com and re-sign with a test key if the app owns a dev keypair.
variants.expect: Must 401 — exact match, not suffix or substring.
variants.why: String-contains issuer checks fall to domain-lookalike values.

variants.name: Missing iss
variants.payload: Remove iss entirely from a re-signed test token.
variants.expect: Must 401; absence of issuer is not "default issuer".
variants.why: Optional-looking claims must still be required.

checks.title: Audience bound to this service
checks.why: Tokens are minted for an audience; a token for service A must not open doors in service B.
checks.validate: aud contains this service client id / resource id; anything else is 401.

variants.name: Cross-service token
variants.payload: Use an access token obtained for the profile API against the billing API (both first-party).
variants.expect: Billing must 401/403. Record which services share audiences.
variants.why: Shared audiences quietly collapse service boundaries.

variants.name: aud omitted
variants.payload: Re-sign a test token with aud removed.
variants.expect: Must 401; no aud means no proof the token was issued for you.
variants.why: Missing-audience acceptance turns any issuer token into a master key.

variants.name: aud array with extras
variants.payload: aud as an array containing your id plus unrelated values.
variants.expect: Acceptable only if policy allows; every listed audience must be known. Unknown value => 401.
variants.why: Array audiences widen blast radius when not constrained.

checks.title: Token type and purpose enforced
checks.why: ID tokens, access tokens, refresh tokens, and email-verification tokens are not interchangeable.
checks.validate: Each endpoint accepts exactly one token type (typ header and/or token-use claim), rejecting the others.

variants.name: ID token at the API
variants.payload: Take the OIDC ID token from login and send it as Authorization: Bearer against a first-party API.
variants.expect: Must 401. ID tokens are for the client, not for APIs.
variants.why: The classic OIDC confusion: ID tokens assert identity, not API access.

variants.name: Access token at userinfo-as-email-verify
variants.payload: Use a normal access token where the app expects its email-verification or magic-link token.
variants.expect: Must fail; purpose-bound tokens carry a distinguishing use/purpose claim.
variants.why: Purpose confusion lets a low-value token do a high-value job.

variants.name: typ header swap
variants.payload: Re-sign with typ changed between JWT and at+jwt across endpoints.
variants.expect: Consistent behaviour: the server enforces the typ it documents, or rejects unknown typ.
variants.why: typ is a cheap purpose tag; ignoring it removes the first line of separation.

checks.title: Subject and tenant claims bound to authority
checks.why: Identity must come from verified token claims, never from client-controlled parameters layered on top.
checks.validate: The acting identity equals the verified sub/oid, and tenant context derives from token claims only.

variants.name: Parameter identity override
variants.payload: With a valid token for account A on tenant 1, call the same endpoint with ?userId=<account-B>&tenantId=2 style overrides.
variants.expect: Responses must stay inside account A / tenant 1. Parameter-driven identity is an authorization bypass.
variants.why: Token says who you are; the request must not get a vote.

variants.name: Cross-tenant same-sub
variants.payload: Where sub ids are emails/GUIDs shared across tenants, use tenant-1 token against tenant-2 object ids.
variants.expect: Must 403 — tenant must come from the token, not the URL.
variants.why: Global identifiers make tenant binding the only guardrail.

variants.name: Conflicting claims
variants.payload: Craft (with the app-owned dev key) sub=A with oid/tenant claims of B.
variants.expect: Rejected or resolved consistently toward the authoritative identity claim per documented policy.
variants.why: Conflicting identity claims must have a defined winner, not first-parsed.

checks.title: Replay limited by token risk
checks.why: Bearer tokens replay by design within lifetime; one-time and step-up tokens must not.
checks.validate: One-time tokens (magic link, email verify, step-up) fail on second use; access tokens document an intended lifetime.

variants.name: Magic-link double spend
variants.payload: Use a magic-link JWT twice, in two sessions.
variants.expect: Second use must fail; the jti must be single-use server-side.
variants.why: A link that keeps giving is persistent access from one interception.

variants.name: Step-up re-use after timeout
variants.payload: Complete a step-up (re-auth or MFA) flow, capture its short-lived confirmation token, replay after the documented window.
variants.expect: Must 401 once expired; window should be minutes.
variants.why: Step-up assertions are the highest-value replay target.

variants.name: Lifetime note
variants.payload: Record access-token lifetime (exp - iat) and whether revocation is claimed.
variants.expect: Lifetime matches policy (typically <= 60 min) or is documented; note revocation story for the report.
variants.why: Replay risk is lifetime x revocability — measure both.

checks.title: Refresh tokens rotate and revoke as families
checks.why: Stolen refresh tokens are indefinite access; rotation plus family revocation on reuse is the control.
checks.validate: Each refresh use returns a new token, the old one dies, and reuse of a rotated token revokes the whole family.

variants.name: Rotated-token replay
variants.payload: Exchange refresh token R1 for R2, then present R1 again (from a "stolen" second client).
variants.expect: R1 must fail AND the family (R2) must be revoked; log the reuse event.
variants.why: Reuse detection only helps if it burns the thief and owner alike, forcing re-auth.

variants.name: Parallel refresh race
variants.payload: Fire two refresh calls with the same token simultaneously (Repeater parallel groups, 2-3 requests max).
variants.expect: At most one succeeds; the others fail and the loser path must not issue parallel families.
variants.why: Rotation under race must stay linearizable.

variants.name: Unbounded lifetime
variants.payload: Inspect exp/absolute lifetime on refresh tokens and idle policy.
variants.expect: Refresh lifetime is bounded (e.g. 14-90 days absolute) or requires re-auth; immortal refresh tokens are a finding.
variants.why: Long-lived bearer material needs a sunset.

checks.title: Browser token storage matches authority
checks.why: Where the browser keeps tokens decides what XSS can reach: memory < httpOnly cookie < localStorage.
checks.validate: Short-lived access tokens only in memory or httpOnly; no long-lived or refresh tokens in web storage.

variants.name: Storage sweep
variants.payload: DevTools → Application: inventory localStorage, sessionStorage, and cookies on the authed app for tokens.
variants.expect: Access token in memory (or httpOnly cookie) only; refresh tokens never in web storage.
variants.why: A five-minute inventory that maps the XSS blast radius.

variants.name: Readable-script check
variants.payload: In the console on the app origin, read the keys you found and decode any JWT-looking value.
variants.expect: Any stored token readable by script is reportable with its lifetime and scope.
variants.why: Demonstrates the exact primitive an XSS would use.

variants.name: Logout residue
variants.payload: Log out fully, re-run the storage sweep.
variants.expect: All tokens removed; nothing persists for the next origin visitor or after session end.
variants.why: Logout that leaves bearer material is a common miss.

jwt-none.purpose: Signing an arbitrary payload with alg=none and an empty signature bypasses verification.
jwt-none.payload: Header: {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}\nPayload: copy a real token's claims, keep sub\nSignature: (empty)

jwt-role-claim.purpose: A forged role/tenant claim that is honoured is an authorization bypass.
jwt-role-claim.payload: If alg=none or confusion worked, set role=admin / isAdmin=true / tenant_id of B and call an admin route.
